verdict.summary: cartservice became slow — its Redis backing store (redis-cart) stopped responding promptly, so cart reads/writes queued and every caller waited on them.
verdict.reasoning: cartservice, frontend and loadgenerator all trip at the same instant, with checkoutservice following 15s later — that ordering is the shape of a leaf slowing down and the latency travelling up the call chain (cart -> frontend -> loadgenerator, and cart -> checkout for the checkout path). frontend and loadgenerator are pure callers and checkout is a caller of cart, so the only member of the alerting set that is not simply waiting on someone else is cartservice. cartservice's own dependency, redis-cart, is explicitly absent from the instrumented graph, which is exactly where an invisible source of latency would hide: a slow or memory-pressured Redis, or a stalled connection pool to it, makes cartservice latency spike without any downstream service alerting. The wide blast radius (adservice, currencyservice, shipping, etc.) is graph traversal, not evidence that those services are implicated — none of them alerted.
open_questions: redis-cart latency, memory usage/eviction stats and whether it was restarted or failed over around 08:10
cartservice p99 broken down into redis call time vs in-process time — does the wait sit in the Redis client?
cartservice connection-pool saturation, goroutine/thread counts and GC pauses at onset
any deploy or config change to cartservice or its Redis connection string/timeouts in the hour before onset
whether frontend latency is confined to cart-touching endpoints (cart, checkout) or is uniform across all routes
